page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 8 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.8 GHz, the instance allocates 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core on a dedicated basis. The processor architecture includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AES cryptography, though it lacks AMX and AVX512_BF16 capabilities. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across standard compute workloads, alongside notable memory constraints. The instance achieves average scores in stress-ng single-core (1409.67) and multi-core (7430.34) tests, as well as average results in Geekbench single-core (1138.0) and Passmark CPU (8305.34) evaluations. However, multi-threaded performance is constrained, as evidenced by a weak Geekbench multi-core score of 4336.0 and weak bzip3 decompression speeds. Memory performance is also a key tradeoff; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 412.9 GB/sec, the overall Passmark memory score is weak, and the 1.0 GB of RAM per core limits memory-intensive applications.

With its high vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the n2-highcpu-8 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints. It demonstrates average throughput in static web serving (6.62 GB/sec), Redis SET operations (7.13 million operations per second), and Passmark database operations. Additionally, it handles small-scale LLM inference adequately, processing 415.57 prompt tokens per second on a 135M model. This makes the instance suitable for web serving, software compilation, lightweight database operations, and basic text processing, whereas memory-heavy databases or large-scale data science jobs are restricted by the 8 GB memory limit.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM, yielding a low 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon processor with 4 physical cores, it supports AVX-512 and AES instructions but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks place this instance in the average tier for single-core processing, static web serving, and Redis operations, though it exhibits weak multi-core scaling and memory performance in synthetic tests. Qualitatively, the instance provides a resource-dense configuration for compute-heavy, low-memory workloads. It is best suited for web serving, software compilation, and lightweight database tasks rather than memory-intensive applications.
